meta.title: Ants Are Everywhere
meta.textType: the main topic of a text

paragraphs: Ants Are Everywhere, posted by Mia. The Explorers visited the science museum, and Guide Ann gave a talk about ants. She drew a big picture of an ant on the blackboard. She spoke slowly and clearly, so everybody understood. Guide Ann works at the museum, and she loves insects. I wrote the facts in my notebook, and here they are.

Topic one: where ants live. Ants live almost everywhere in the world. They live in forests, in gardens, and even in our houses. Many ants make a nest under the ground. Some ants make a nest in a tree. Only very cold places have no ants. Ants are small, but there are very many of them.

Topic two: how ants work. An ant is a small insect, but it is very strong. It can carry a leaf that is bigger than its body. Ants work together, so the work is not too hard. Ants do not talk, but they use smells. A smell can say, "Follow me!" Every nest has a queen, and she is the mother of all the ants. The other ants find food and look after the nest.

Topic three: how scientists study ants. A scientist watches ants for many hours. She uses a small camera to see inside the nest. She writes what she sees in a notebook, and she counts the ants. Then she puts the facts online, so other scientists can read them. Scientists in different countries share what they learn. Guide Ann said, "A good scientist is a good watcher." Maybe one of us will be a scientist, too.

Topic four: what the club can do. Guide Ann gave us a small job for the next week. It is easy, and it needs only a notebook and a pencil. We will show our facts at the club on Thursday. Every Explorer must watch ants for ten minutes and write three facts. Leo wants to watch the ants at the school gate. I will watch the ants in my garden, and I will take a photo. Where will you watch ants?
text.summary: Mia writes a fact page about ants for Explorers' Blog. Each paragraph has one topic. The topics are the talk at the museum, where ants live, how they work, and how scientists study them.
